metadata.title: How OTA Encryption Meets App Store Compliance
metadata.description: Explore how OTA encryption secures app updates and ensures compliance with stringent app store regulations.
metadata.author: Martin Donadieu

blocks.text: Over-the-Air (OTA) encryption ensures secure app updates while meeting the strict rules of Apple and Google app stores.
Here's how it works and why it's essential:
: Encryption blocks data interception, tampering, and unauthorized access during update delivery.
: A highly secure encryption standard with 256-bit keys for robust data protection.
: Updates are encrypted from creation to installation, ensuring integrity and device-specific decryption.

Modern OTA update systems use layered encryption techniques to maintain security and comply with app store standards. These methods protect updates throughout their creation, delivery, and installation processes.

(TLS) is the backbone of secure OTA update delivery. It meets important requirements like Apple's ATS and Google's SSL pinning by establishing an encrypted connection between servers and devices. This prevents data from being intercepted or tampered with during transmission.
Here’s how TLS features align with security and compliance needs:
Safeguards past communications if keys are compromised
These transport-layer measures serve as the first line of defense, while end-to-end encryption secures updates throughout their lifecycle.

End-to-end encryption ensures updates remain secure from the moment they’re created to when they’re installed. This approach satisfies app store requirements for safeguarding sensitive data at all stages.
Key elements of end-to-end encryption include:
: Updates are encrypted before they leave the source.
: Data is transmitted through TLS-protected channels.
: Only the target device, using securely stored keys, can decrypt the updates.
AES-256 encryption is a standard that meets the encryption requirements for both iOS and Android platforms.
"AES-256 is one of the most secure encryption algorithms available, approved by the U.S. National Security Agency for top secret information"
: With 2^256 possible combinations, brute-force attacks are virtually impossible
: Supported natively on both iOS and Android platforms.
